q1.answer: ADR013 (use node-fetch) is superseded and no longer in force. It was replaced by ADR014, which says frontend plugins and packages should prefer the `fetchApiRef` (injected via `useApi`), which is exactly what NotificationsClient does by accepting fetchApi in its constructor instead of importing fetch/node-fetch/cross-fetch directly.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires any fetch/XMLHttpRequest in tests to be mocked with msw (setupServer/setupWorker + http.get handlers). It frames the problem as every test type (unit to e2e) otherwise having its own ad-hoc implementation of mocking requests, i.e. it avoids each test reinventing its own mocking approach and avoids mocking `fetch` directly (as react-testing-library itself recommends against).

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly added a `children` prop even when not wanted, and that it did not support a generic type on children. It notes that Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript template as a concrete fact about why it fell out of favor upstream.

q4.answer: The ADR names Moment.js as the library being replaced by Luxon, citing two reasons it's being retired: Moment.js suffers from large bundle size and mutable-state issues, and separately the Moment.js project itself is being sunset/deprecated by its own maintainers.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to src/index.ts, with each index file only re-exporting its immediate children. This was meant to make it easy to answer questions like "Is this export also exported by the package?" and "What is exported from this directory?"

q6.answer: No, under ADR004's rule they are not part of the public API: the rule says a symbol is only exported if every index file in the chain up to src/index.ts re-exports it, and if any link is missing (here there's no src/utils/index.ts at all, and src/index.ts never mentions these files) the symbol must be considered not publicly exported, even with no explicit 'private' marker.

q7.answer: ADR011 says `x-react` packages are for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself (`x`) AND third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a `notifications-react` package, other frontend plugins would have to want to reuse its components/hooks directly rather than only notifications itself using them.

q8.answer: ADR003 allows a default export only when 'absolutely necessary', giving React.lazy modules as that one exception (React.lazy's dynamic import expects a default export). The workaround for teams avoiding even that is to wrap the dynamic import with `.then(m => ({ default: m.Component }))` to synthesize a default from a named export.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the `loader`/`component` option pattern for providing JSX elements/components. Its Consequences section says it will be applied to update all APIs for the new frontend system (`@backstage/frontend-*` packages) but explicitly will NOT be retrofitted onto existing APIs for the old frontend system (`@backstage/core-*` packages), which is the style the dev app (and NotificationsPage wiring) already uses.
